title: Smartphone Quiz: Can You Get 5/5?
hook: You use your phone all day. But can you ace this quiz? Let's find out!

questions.q: Which company makes Galaxy phones?
questions.explain: Samsung's Galaxy line launched back in 2009.

questions.q: Which app has a white ghost on a yellow logo?
questions.explain: The ghost logo is nicknamed Ghostface Chillah.

questions.q: Which company owns Instagram?
questions.explain: Facebook bought Instagram for about one billion dollars.

questions.q: What year did the first iPhone go on sale?
questions.explain: It went on sale in the US in June 2007.

questions.q: What does USB stand for?
questions.explain: USB first arrived in 1996.

outro: How many did you get right? Comment your score!
description: Five quick questions about smartphones and the apps you use every day.
sources: Apple Newsroom — iPhone on sale June 29, 2007

title: Internet History Quiz: 5 Questions
hook: Think you know the internet? These five questions say otherwise. Let's go!

questions.q: Which company bought YouTube in 2006?
questions.explain: Google paid 1.65 billion dollars in stock.
questions.note: Google bought YouTube in Nov 2006 for $1.65B

questions.q: What year was Google founded?
questions.explain: It started in a garage in Menlo Park, California.

questions.q: Who co-founded Microsoft with Bill Gates?
questions.explain: Gates and Allen were childhood friends from Seattle.
questions.note: Microsoft was founded in 1975 by Gates & Allen

questions.q: What was the first video ever uploaded to YouTube?
questions.explain: It's just 19 seconds long, filmed at San Diego Zoo.
questions.note: Uploaded April 23, 2005 by co-founder Jawed Karim

questions.q: What does HTTP stand for?
questions.explain: It's how your browser fetches web pages.

outro: So, what's your score out of five? Tell me below!
description: Five questions about the history of the internet, Google, Microsoft and YouTube.

title: Space Quiz: Only Space Nerds Get 5/5
hook: Five space questions. Only real space nerds get all five. Ready?

questions.q: Which planet is called the Red Planet?
questions.explain: Its red color comes from rusty iron in the dust.
questions.note: Iron oxide on the surface. Source: NASA

questions.q: Which company builds the Starship rocket?
questions.explain: Starship is the biggest rocket ever flown.

questions.q: What's NASA's program to send humans back to the Moon?
questions.explain: Artemis is named after Apollo's twin sister in myths.
questions.note: Source: NASA. Orion is the crew capsule Artemis uses

questions.q: Which space telescope launched in December 2021?
questions.explain: Webb sees the universe in infrared light.

questions.q: About how long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
questions.explain: So you're always seeing the Sun as it was 8 minutes ago.
questions.note: About 8 min 20 s on average; it varies slightly. Source: NASA

outro: How many did you get? Comment your score, space nerds!
description: Five space questions, from Mars to the James Webb Space Telescope.
sources: NASA — James Webb Space Telescope (launched Dec 25, 2021)

title: Brand Quiz: Can You Get All 5?
hook: You see these brands every day. But do you really know them? Let's test you!

questions.q: Which company makes the PlayStation?
questions.explain: The first PlayStation launched in 1994.

questions.q: Which company makes the Model 3 car?
questions.explain: The Model 3 is one of the best-selling electric cars.

questions.q: What did Amazon first sell online?
questions.explain: Amazon started as an online bookstore.

questions.q: Which studio originally created Minecraft?
questions.explain: Mojang is the Swedish studio behind Minecraft.

questions.q: In NFT, what does the N stand for?
questions.explain: NFT means non-fungible token.
questions.note: A unique digital token that can't be swapped one-for-one

outro: So, did you get all five? Drop your score below!
description: Five quick questions about famous brands and where they came from.

title: Everyday Science Quiz: 5/5 or Not?
hook: Five science questions you learned in school. Bet you forgot one. Let's go!

questions.q: What gas do plants absorb from the air?
questions.explain: Plants use it to make food in photosynthesis.
questions.note: Plants take in CO2 and release oxygen

questions.q: What's the hardest natural substance?
questions.explain: Diamond scores a perfect 10 on the Mohs scale.
questions.note: Hardest natural material; some lab-made materials are harder

questions.q: What's the chemical symbol for gold?
questions.explain: Au comes from aurum, the Latin word for gold.
questions.note: Ag is silver, from the Latin 'argentum'

questions.q: How many bones does an adult human have?
questions.explain: Babies start with more, and some fuse as they grow.
questions.note: Typical adult count; babies have around 300

questions.q: About how fast does light travel?
questions.explain: That's fast enough to circle Earth over 7 times a second.

outro: How many did you get? Be honest, comment your score!
description: Five everyday science questions — photosynthesis, diamonds, gold, bones and the speed of light.

title: Gaming Quiz: True Gamers Get 5/5
hook: Calling all gamers. Five questions. Only true gamers get them all. Let's go!

questions.q: Which company makes the Xbox?
questions.explain: The first Xbox came out in 2001.

questions.q: What does NPC stand for?
questions.explain: Characters the game controls, not a real player.
questions.note: A term from tabletop role-playing games

questions.q: What year did Fortnite come out?
questions.explain: Battle Royale mode dropped a few months later.

questions.q: What year did the original PlayStation launch in Japan?
questions.explain: It reached the US and Europe in 1995.

questions.q: Which game has sold about 400 million copies?
questions.explain: It's the best-selling single game of all time.
questions.note: As of 2026. Tetris tops this if you count all its versions combined

outro: So how many did you get, gamer? Comment your score!
description: Five gaming questions, from Xbox and PlayStation to the best-selling game ever.
sources: Wikipedia: List of best-selling video games (Minecraft ~400M as of 2026; Tetris 520M across versions)
